hints.title: Solve for sine and cosine first
hints.body: Give sin(2x) and cos(2x) short names. Solve the resulting two linear equations by elimination.
hints.recap: Two trigonometric values can be treated as algebraic unknowns initially.
hints.pitfall: Both equations must hold for the same angle.
hints.pause: Find both values and check them in the two equations.

recall.reminder: Multiply and add or subtract two linear equations to eliminate one unknown.

hints.title: Use both signs to select angles
hints.body: Use the two values you found to locate the angle in the correct quadrant. Find every such angle in the full interval for 2x.
hints.recap: The signs of sine and cosine together identify the quadrant.
hints.pitfall: When the angle is doubled, double both ends of its search interval.

recall.reminder: Transform the whole angle interval and check its endpoints.

hints.title: Return to the requested variable
hints.body: Convert every doubled angle back to x and add those x-values.
hints.recap: The trigonometric input and the original variable are not the same quantity.
hints.pitfall: Check the stated endpoints rather than adding an extra full turn automatically.

recall.reminder: After solving for a changed angle, return to the original variable.

solution:
Writing S=sin(2x), C=cos(2x), multiply 3S−C=3 by 3 and add S+3C=−1. This gives 4S=2, hence S=12 and C=−32.

Both hold when 2x=150∘ or 510∘ within [0∘,720∘]. Therefore x=75∘ or 255∘.

The sum is 330∘, answer B. The degree unit applies to the angle; keeping the doubled input separate from x prevents the distractor 660∘.
knowledgePattern: Solve for sine and cosine together then enforce both phase conditions
